records.quote: CDFs are investigated here using a spherical porous burner with gaseous fuels in the microgravity environment of the International Space Station. Normal and inverse flames burning ethane, propane, and n-butane were explored with various fuel and oxygen concentrations, pressures, and flow rates.
records.derivation: Covers both normal and inverse flames (second sentence). The sentences come from the abstract of Kim et al., 'Spherical Gas-Fueled Cool Diffusion Flames', Proc. Combust. Inst. (2022), doi:10.1016/j.proci.2022.07.015, reproduced in section 4.C of the Final Report. Not used as gravity evidence: the project name 'Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments' and the PSI label projectType 'Microgravity Investigation' (record text).

records.test_id: ground-based pool-flame tests (not ISS; no NASA test id; not in PSI tables)
records.quote: Cool diffusion flames burning near the surface of fuel pools in normal gravity were observed for the first time.
records.derivation: Applies ONLY to a separate ground experiment (liquid n-heptane pool between heated plates; abstract on page 23, see R5), listed as an 'Additional Objective'. These are not CFI-G ISS burner tests and must not be attached to any row of the PSI-159 tables.

records.quote: Flames of Gaseous Fuels
records.derivation: PSI sub-research-area label of the investigation (a label, not a sentence about specific tests); corroborated by R4.

records.quote: CDFs are investigated here using a spherical porous burner with gaseous fuels in the microgravity environment of the International Space Station. Normal and inverse flames burning ethane, propane, and n-butane were explored with various fuel and oxygen concentrations, pressures, and flow rates.
records.derivation: Fuels are gases (ethane, propane, n-butane) fed through a porous spherical burner (normal flames) or filled into the chamber (inverse flames); there are no material samples in this investigation.

records.test_id: ground-based pool-flame tests (not ISS; no NASA test id; not in PSI tables)
records.quote: A method is presented here for observing CDFs inexpensively using a pool of liquid n-heptane and parallel plates heated so as to produce a stably stratified stagnation flow.
records.derivation: Same separate ground experiment as R2; not a CFI-G ISS test.

ACME, Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

records.quote: The Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G) experiment is one of six independent experiments that make up the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project for which the tests were conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).

The Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (CFI-G) experiment is one of six independent experiments that make up the Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (ACME) project for which the tests were conducted within the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) on the International Space Station (ISS).
records.derivation: Shared with the other five ACME experiments (see lineage).

records.quote: Atmosphere, diluted by nitrogen in all cases, is only nominal where the pressure increases and O2% drops with vitiation.
records.derivation: STREAM: AMBIENT (chamber atmosphere), NORMAL flames, first round (footnote 2 of Table 1). Oxygen balanced by nitrogen. test_id lists the Test Day ids of Table 1; individual PSI test ids begin with these 5 digits (e.g. 21088A1).

records.quote: Although it was in the second round, the final day of CFI-G testing was carried out in the normal flame configuration, with gaseous fuel (with or without nitrogen) flowing into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere.
records.derivation: STREAM: AMBIENT, NORMAL flames, final test day 21291 (second round). Oxygen balanced by nitrogen.

records.value_original: a mixture of nitrogen and gaseous fuel
records.quote: The inverse flame tests were conducted with the chamber filled with a mixture of nitrogen and gaseous fuel while an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowed from the burner.
records.derivation: STREAM: AMBIENT (chamber), INVERSE flames. Here nitrogen balances the FUEL; the ambient contains no oxygen. The oxygen-balancing diluent of inverse flames is in the burner stream (R13). test_id = the 12 inverse-flame Test Days of Table 2 (page 22).

records.quote: The inverse flame tests were conducted with the chamber filled with a mixture of nitrogen and gaseous fuel while an oxygen/nitrogen mixture flowed from the burner.
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (oxidizer issued from the porous sphere), INVERSE flames. Oxygen balanced by nitrogen. The burner O2 fraction itself is in the PSI table and is not extracted here.

records.quote: Atmosphere, diluted by nitrogen in all cases, is only nominal where the pressure increases and O2% drops with vitiation.
records.derivation: STREAM: AMBIENT, all Table 2 test days (footnote 2 of Table 2). For the 12 inverse days the 'Atmosphere' column lists fuel concentrations, so nitrogen balances the FUEL there; for 21291 (normal flames) the atmosphere is O2 balanced by nitrogen.

records.quote: On GMT 088, the first test points were performed for ACME CFI-G Part 1 (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases) with 14 ethane flames, sometimes diluted with nitrogen, ignited in various oxygen/nitrogen atmospheres.
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. 'sometimes': only the diluted tests of that day have a burner diluent (Table 1 lists the 21088 bottle as 100% C2H6). test_id from GMT day: GMT 088 of 2021 = Test Day 21088 (Table 1 footnote 1: year as first two digits followed by the 3-digit day of the year).

records.quote: On GMT 102, nine nitrogen-diluted butane flames were ignited for ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases).
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 102 of 2021 = Test Day 21102.

records.quote: On GMT 106, additional tests were performed with nitrogen-diluted butane for ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases).
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 106 of 2021 = Test Day 21106.

records.quote: On GMT 125, ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases) test points were performed using nitrogen-diluted butane fuel at both elevated and normal oxygen concentrations.
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 125 of 2021 = Test Day 21125.

records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 130 of 2021 = Test Day 21130.

records.quote: On GMT 137, ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases) test points were performed using nitrogen-diluted propane fuel in elevated oxygen concentrations (about 40%).
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 137 of 2021 = Test Day 21137.

records.quote: On GMT 153, 14 nitrogen-diluted ethane flames were ignited for ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases) in atmospheres ranging between 30-40% oxygen with pressures of both 0.5 and 2 atm.

records.quote: On GMT 174, we ignited 16 nitrogen-diluted butane flames in the final tests for the first round of ACME CFI-G (Cool Flames Investigation with Gases).
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames. GMT 174 of 2021 = Test Day 21174.

records.quote: Although it was in the second round, the final day of CFI-G testing was carried out in the normal flame configuration, with gaseous fuel (with or without nitrogen) flowing into an oxygen/nitrogen atmosphere.
records.derivation: STREAM: BURNER (fuel), NORMAL flames, final test day 21291. 'with or without': N2 is the only fuel diluent named; tests with undiluted fuel have no burner diluent (Table 2, page 22, lists the 21291 bottle as '30% n-C4H10 with N2').

records.test_id: Fig. 1 flames (a), (b), (c): normal n-butane flames, test ids not given in the caption
records.quote: These flames involve 30 vol% n-butane flowing at 1.5 mg/s into (a) 37.9, (b) 39.5, and (c) 39.9 vol% O2 at 300 K.
records.derivation: Read from the Fig. 1 caption text, not from the plot. The 300 K is stated only for the three example flames of Fig. 1; 'at 300 K' attaches to the O2 atmosphere but could also be read as the temperature of both reactants. Possible matches with Table 3 (page 46) by O2 fraction and flow rate ((b) -> 21174C3, (c) -> 21291A1) are unverified inferences and are NOT used as test_id. No sentence gives the ambient temperature for all tests. The 'T = 300 K' on page 5 is a representative value in the 2017 proposal's Richardson-number estimate, not a test condition, and was not used.

not_found.looked_in: Burner (fuel) stream for normal-flame Test Day 21112 (Table 1 bottle 100% C3H8): record text (all sections); Final Report PDF pages 3, 21, 39, 48, 53 (GMT 112 summary says only 'propane fuel'), 73. Whether that day's fuel was diluted on orbit, and with what, is not stated in text.

All tests except the three Fig. 1 example flames (R25): record text (all sections); Final Report PDF pages 1-93, including Tables 1-3 (pages 21-22, 39-40, 46), sections 3-4 and Appendices B-H. Only burner, flame and thermocouple temperatures appear elsewhere, plus a representative 'T = 300 K' in the proposal's Richardson-number estimate (page 5), which is not a test condition.

lineage: CFI-G ran in the ACME chamber insert inside the CIR, the single modular hardware set shared with the other ACME experiments (CLD Flame, BRE, E-FIELD Flames, Flame Design, s-Flame): 'The experiment is carried out using the same spherical burner configuration as ACME’s Flame Design and s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames) experiments. The instrumentation is the same as that used for Flame Design except that an alternate radiometer array was developed for CFI-G.' (PDF page 29). The intensified camera came from the earlier CFI droplet experiment (page 30), the 3-fiber TFP array was carried over from BRE/CLD Flame testing (page 16), and report section 3.A is copied from the shared 'ACME Engineering Implementation' document (page 6).
